inventory.purpose: Thin CI consumer for repository documentation obligation receipts.
Canonical Repository Documentation Obligation Compiler front door.
Target resolution, obligation lifecycle, validation, and terminal-status derivation.

ownership_boundaries.responsibility: discover and qualify semantic evidence only

must_not_own: module README rendering duplicated from readme-pipeline-v1

evidence.claim: The existing governance-self-check workflow invokes repo_docs.py, passes source-head and tested-revision identity, exposes obligation counts, and uploads the receipt.
repo_docs.py is the machine-first Repository Documentation Obligation Compiler and delegates semantic qualification to l9-intelligence-harvest.
Documentation obligations are target-resolved, validated individually, and receipt status is derived from whether required obligations are terminal or blocked.
DocumentationObligation is a first-class typed machine contract with target, owner, trigger, revision, qualification, action, evidence, lifecycle, validation, and blockers.

concepts.name: Repository documentation obligation compiler architecture
concepts.description: Repository documentation maintenance is modeled as compilation from repository delta and documentation topology into typed target-resolved obligations, with semantic qualification delegated upstream and owner-native rendering preserved.
concepts.problem: Surface-level stale flags do not provide a durable machine unit with exact target, owner, evidence, lifecycle, and closure semantics.
concepts.semantic_contract: Repository changes compile into target-resolved DocumentationObligation objects; deterministic qualification remains local, semantic qualification remains owned by l9-intelligence-harvest, specialist owners render their own targets, and CI consumes the resulting receipt rather than reimplementing the compiler.
risks: Duplicating semantic reasoning inside Repo Docs would create a second Harvest owner.
Moving rendering into the compiler would create duplicate documentation owners.

acceptance_tests.given: a repository change impacts one or more documentation surfaces
acceptance_tests.then: it emits target-resolved DocumentationObligation objects and a receipt
acceptance_tests.must_not: collapse owner-specific work back into surface-only stale flags or duplicate specialist renderers

beneficiary_fit.merge_decision: refresh the architecture index with the executable compiler boundary

concepts.name: Evidence-backed terminal documentation closure
concepts.description: Receipt PASS is a derived result of per-obligation terminality and required validation, not a separate optimistic status plane.
concepts.problem: Independent surface, freshness, capability, and semantic status planes can disagree and allow false completion claims.
concepts.semantic_contract: A repository documentation receipt may report PASS only when every applicable DocumentationObligation is terminal with required validation evidenced; any required non-terminal obligation remains PARTIAL, any blocked obligation yields BLOCKED, and semantic obligations may close only after change-bound canonical Harvest evidence is admitted.
risks: Treating SATISFIED as terminal would equate a touched target with validated closure.
Accepting unbound Harvest evidence would allow semantic proof from the wrong repository change.

acceptance_tests.given: one or more applicable documentation obligations exist
acceptance_tests.then: PASS occurs only after all required obligations are terminal and validated
acceptance_tests.must_not: report PASS while any required obligation is awaiting qualification, open, validated-but-nonterminal, handoff-required, or blocked

beneficiary_fit.merge_decision: add the executable closure and Harvest-binding invariant pointers
